question.problem:
Consider the following data sets:

$$
x=\{13,\,4,\,10\},\,y=\{0,\,-3,\,9\}
$$

You are given that $\overset{―}{x}=9$ and $\overset{―}{y}=2.$ Calculate the corresponding linear correlation coefficient. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The linear correlation coefficient $\rho $ of the data sets $x=\{{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}\}$ and $y=\{{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}\}$ is given by 

$$
\rho (x,y)=\frac{\text{Cov}(x,y)}{{\sigma }_{x}\cdot {\sigma }_{y}}=\frac{{S}_{xy}}{\sqrt{{S}_{xx}\cdot {S}_{yy}}}.
$$

First, we compute the sum in the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =(13-9)(0-2)+(4-9)(-3-2)+(10-9)(9-2) \\  & =(4)(-2)+(-5)(-5)+(1)(7) \\  & =-8+25+7 \\  & =24\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we compute the sums in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =(13-9)^{2}+(4-9)^{2}+(10-9)^{2} \\  & =16+25+1 \\  & =42 \\ {S}_{yy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})^{2} \\  & =(0-2)^{2}+(-3-2)^{2}+(9-2)^{2} \\  & =4+25+49 \\  & =78\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho (x,y) & =\frac{24}{\sqrt{42}\cdot \sqrt{78}} \\  & ≈\frac{24}{6.480\,741\cdot 8.831\,761} \\  & ≈0.42\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
